name: Serie
summary: A terminal application that renders git commit graphs as images using terminal image display protocols, similar to git log --graph --all.
use_cases: browse a git repository's commit graph in the terminal
view git diff output for a commit in a dedicated view
features: render git commit graphs as terminal images

setup.command:
rm -rf /tmp/repo && mkdir -p /tmp/repo && cd /tmp/repo && git init -q -b main && git config user.email a@b.c && git config user.name T && echo 1>f && git add f && git commit -qm first && git checkout -qb feat && echo 2>>f && git commit -qam feat1 && git checkout -q main && echo 3>g && git add g && git commit -qm second && git merge -q --no-ff feat -m merge && git log --oneline --graph --all
cat > /tmp/serie.toml <<'EOF'
[keybind]
quit = ["x"]
user_command_1 = ["u"]

[core.user_command]
commands_1 = { name = "write hash", type = "silent", commands = ["sh", "-c", "echo USERCMD {{target_hash}} > /tmp/uc_out.txt"] }
EOF
cat > /tmp/drive.py <<'EOF'
import os, pty, sys, time, select, struct, fcntl, termios
mode = sys.argv[1]
env = dict(os.environ, TERM="xterm-256color")
if mode != "graph":
    env["SERIE_CONFIG_FILE"] = "/tmp/serie.toml"
try: os.remove("/tmp/uc_out.txt")
except FileNotFoundError: pass
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.chdir("/tmp/repo")
    os.execvpe("serie", ["serie", "-p", "iterm"], env)
fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 40, 120, 800, 1200))
buf = b""
def pump(t):
    global buf
    end = time.time() + t
    while time.time() < end:
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
        if r:
            try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
            except OSError: return
            if not d: return
            buf += d
def alive():
    return os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG) == (0, 0)
pump(3)
ok = True
if mode == "graph":
    n = buf.count(b"\x1b]1337;File=")
    print("iterm_images:", n)
    print("first commit msg shown:", b"merge" in buf)
    ok = n > 0
    os.write(fd, b"q")
elif mode == "keys":
    os.write(fd, b"q"); pump(1.5)
    a = alive(); print("alive after q (rebound):", a); ok = a
    os.write(fd, b"x")
elif mode == "usercmd":
    os.write(fd, b"u"); pump(2)
    out = open("/tmp/uc_out.txt").read().strip() if os.path.exists("/tmp/uc_out.txt") else "NO OUTPUT"
    print("user command output:", out); ok = out.startswith("USERCMD")
    os.write(fd, b"x")
pump(3)
st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
print("exited:", st[0] != 0, "status:", st[1])
if st[0] == 0:
    os.kill(pid, 9); ok = False
print("RESULT", "OK" if ok else "FAIL")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
EOF

pitfalls.actually_needed: No Rust toolchain in the box; used the prebuilt GitHub release tarball serie-0.11.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (the README points to the other download options)

pitfalls.readme_said: The default key bindings can be overridden
pitfalls.actually_needed: Setting quit = ["x"] made x quit, but the default q still quit as well (cmd 8). Custom keys seem to be added to the default keys instead of replacing them.

pitfalls.readme_said: Use a terminal emulator that supports the iTerm2 or kitty image protocol
pitfalls.actually_needed: No real terminal here. serie ran in a pseudo-terminal with -p iterm and sent iTerm2 inline-image sequences, but whether the images display correctly was not seen.

judge.observed: All three checks exited 0 and printed their expected signals: RESULT OK with 4 iterm images rendered, the custom x key quit serie, and the version reads serie 0.11.0.
